e-9454.knowledge_point: Calculating the Force Acting on a Body Given Its Velocity
e-9454.problem:
A body of mass $3 \, \textrm{kg}$ is moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis under the action of a single force $F,$ measured in Newtons $(\textrm{N}).$
At time $t$ seconds, the velocity of the body is given by $v(t) =t^2- e^{t-4}$ meters per second.
Calculate the magnitude of the force at time $t=4$ seconds.
e-9454.worked_solution:
According to Newton’s second law

$$
F=ma,
$$

 
where $F$ is the force, $m$ is the mass, and $a$ is the acceleration.

To find the acceleration $a(t),$ we differentiate the velocity $v(t){:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-{e}^{t-4}) \\  & =2t-{e}^{t-4}\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, the acceleration at $t=4 \, \textrm{s}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =2(4)-{e}^{4-4} \\  & =8-1 \\  & =7\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the force, in Newtons, is

$$
\begin{aligned}F & =ma \\  & =3\cdot (7) \\  & =21.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the magnitude of the force is

$$
|F| = |21| = 21 \, \textrm{N}.
$$

after.name: Question 2
after.worked_solution:
By Newton’s second law,

$$
F(t)=ma(t),
$$

where $F(t)$ is the force, $m$ is the mass, and $a(t)$ is the acceleration.

To find the acceleration $a(t),$ we differentiate the velocity $v(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[3\operatorname{cos}⁡({e}^{2t})] \\  & =-3\operatorname{sin}⁡({e}^{2t})\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{2t}) \\  & =-3\operatorname{sin}⁡({e}^{2t})\cdot 2{e}^{2t} \\  & =-6{e}^{2t}\operatorname{sin}⁡({e}^{2t}).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the force, in Newtons, is

$$
\begin{aligned}F(t) & =ma(t) \\  & =9\cdot [-6{e}^{2t}\operatorname{sin}⁡({e}^{2t})] \\  & =-54{e}^{2t}\operatorname{sin}⁡({e}^{2t}).\end{aligned}
$$

A body of mass 2kg is moving in a straight line along the x-axis under the action of a single force F, measured in Newtons (N). At time t seconds, the velocity of the body is given by v(t)=sec⁡t meters per second.

Calculate the magnitude of the force at time t=π4 seconds. Do not round the answer.

The magnitude of the force equals
N.
Submit

decision.explanation: Acceleration is v'(t)=sec(t)tan(t). At t=π/4, acceleration equals √2·1=√2. Thus the force magnitude is |ma|=√2·√2=2 N.
